name: Splatting
text:
# Splatting


## Overview
Splatting is an [object-order volume rendering](#10725-object-order-volume-rendering.md) technique where volumetric data is decomposed into primitives (typically Gaussians or disks) that are projected onto the image plane as overlapping footprints and accumulated via [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) [S2, unofficial][S4, unofficial][S7, unofficial]. It solves the problem of efficiently rendering dense volumetric data by leveraging hardware-accelerated rasterization and cache-coherent traversal, contrasting with [image-order ray-casting](#3161-image-order-ray-casting.md) which samples the volume per-pixel [S2, unofficial][S14, unofficial]. Unlike [Shear-warp](24-shear-warp.md), which relies on affine warping of slices, splatting handles perspective distortion through per-primitive footprint calculation (e.g., EWA) or sheet-buffer [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) [S4, unofficial][S11, abstract only, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The splatting family shares the fundamental mechanism of treating volumetric data as a set of geometric or parametric primitives that are transformed and rasterized [S1, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial].

1.  **[Primitive Representation](#11838-primitive-representation.md):** The volume is decomposed into primitives [G]. Each primitive $k$ is defined by its position $\mathbf{p}_k$, density/extinction coefficient $g_k$ or $\rho_k$, and a reconstruction kernel $h$ (typically a Gaussian) [S1, unofficial][S6, unofficial][S10, unofficial].
2.  **Transformation:** Primitives are transformed from volume space to screen space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix or specific factorizations [S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial]. For perspective projections, the kernel shape may be distorted (e.g., [EWA splatting](#1069-ewa-splatting.md)) to account for foreshortening [S6, unofficial][S10, unofficial].
3.  **Rasterization:** The transformed primitives are projected onto the 2D image plane [G]. The contribution of a voxel $D$ to a screen point $(x,y)$ is determined by the [footprint function](#4731-footprint-function-mechanism.md) $F(x,y)$, which is the integral of the 3D kernel along the view direction [S2, unofficial][S6, unofficial][S10, unofficial]:
    $$ F(x,y) = \int h(x-x_D, y-y_D, z) \, dz $$
    The intensity written to the pixel is modulated by the voxel density:
    $$ P(x,y) = \text{weight}(x,y) \cdot \rho(D) $$
4.  **Compositing:** Contributions are accumulated to form the final image [G]. This is typically done using alpha blending in back-to-front or front-to-back order to handle transparency correctly [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial][S7, unofficial]. Splatting compositing is performed along sheets (all pixels at once for a set of voxels), whereas ray-casting composites along rays (one sample at a time) [S10, unofficial].
5.  **Hardware [Acceleration](#18-acceleration.md):** Most methods in this family rely on GPU rasterization pipelines for performance, enabling real-time interactivity [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Splatting Without the Blur](1157-splatting-without-the-blur.md)
[Splatting Without the Blur](#1157-splatting-without-the-blur.md) performs [classification and shading](#2278-classification-and-shading.md) in screen space after voxels are projected, avoiding edge blurring from pre-shaded splatting. It distinguishes itself from pre-classified methods by deferring optical property computation until after density footprint rasterization.

### [Rendering Pipelines and Passes](1411-rendering-pipelines-and-passes.md)
[Rendering Pipelines and Passes](#1411-rendering-pipelines-and-passes.md) organize volume rendering tasks into sequential logical blocks, separating geometric projection from visual appearance. It solves the problem of managing complex data transformations by decomposing rendering into reusable passes (e.g., attribute accumulation, depth occlusion, normalization).

### [Anti-Aliasing and Filtering](1574-anti-aliasing-and-filtering.md)
This family addresses aliasing artifacts in object-order splatting by modifying splat footprints, opacity, or rendering pipelines to account for spatial and temporal undersampling. It solves the problem of high-frequency content causing flickering and moiré patterns.

### [Slice-by-Slice (Sheet Buffer) Splatting](2110-slice-by-slice-sheet-buffer-splatting.md)
Slice-by-Slice Splatting improves image quality over standard list-based accumulation by organizing splats into 2D cache-sheets aligned with the volume axis most parallel to the image plane. It composites these sheets slice-by-slice in depth order, addressing "sparkling" artifacts, though it may introduce "popping" artifacts at specific view angles.

### [Ultrafast Spatial Texture-Atlas Splatting](3245-ultrafast-spatial-texture-atlas-splatting.md)
[Ultrafast Spatial Texture-Atlas Splatting](#3245-ultrafast-spatial-texture-atlas-splatting.md) eliminates runtime neural network inference by baking view-independent high-frequency texture into a hardware-accelerated 2D texture atlas. It represents the scene as a sparse set of oriented 2D [Beta kernels](#10589-universal-beta-splatting-ubs.md), achieving faster rendering than 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) by reducing overdraw.

### [Lighting and Material Interaction](3851-lighting-and-material-interaction.md)
This family defines how photometric properties and illumination are computed for splatted primitives, addressing the gap between raw geometric density and visually plausible appearance. It decouples the [shading model](#837-shading-models.md) from the rasterization footprint, allowing for dynamic lighting or baked global illumination.

### [Anti-Aliasing for Splatting](4471-anti-aliasing-for-splatting.md)
[Anti-Aliasing for Splatting](#4471-anti-aliasing-for-splatting.md) prevents sample-rate aliasing artifacts during the resampling phase by scaling splat size proportional to the viewing frustum and attenuating splat energy for distant primitives. It specifically addresses ray divergence in perspective projections.

### [Seed Generation for Initial Splats](4634-seed-generation-for-initial-splats.md)
This method generates initial splat positions directly from volumetric data, combining gradient-based sampling for edges (60% of budget) with [uniform grid](#920-uniform-grid.md) sampling for smooth regions (40% of budget) to solve sparse or redundant splat placement.

### [Multi-View Splatting Pipeline with Fill-Rate Filtering](4689-multi-view-splatting-pipeline-with-fill-rate-filtering.md)
This method generates multi-view 2D images from a 3D point cloud by splatting points onto image planes and filtering out sparse views based on fill rate to ensure structured, high-quality outputs.

### [EWA Splatting with kNN Covariance Estimation](4690-ewa-splatting-with-knn-covariance-estimation.md)
[EWA Splatting with kNN Covariance Estimation](#4690-ewa-splatting-with-knn-covariance-estimation.md) treats volumetric data as point primitives, using per-point 3D covariance matrices estimated from k-nearest neighbours to project elliptical weighted average shapes onto the 2D image plane. It solves sparse coverage and aliasing in raw [point cloud rendering](#6750-point-cloud-rendering.md).

### [Hierarchical and Multi-Resolution Splatting](5618-hierarchical-and-multi-resolution-splatting.md)
[Hierarchical and Multi-Resolution Splatting](#5618-hierarchical-and-multi-resolution-splatting.md) optimizes rendering of dense volumetric data by organizing primitives into a [spatial hierarchy](#13154-spatial-hierarchies.md), allowing the renderer to select primitives of varying granularity based on screen-space footprint or error metrics.

### [Splat Texture Layout & Mapping](7089-splat-texture-layout-mapping.md)
[Splat Texture Layout & Mapping](#7089-splat-texture-layout-mapping.md) organizes per-primitive splat data into 3D texture structures to enable efficient GPU-based rendering of Gaussian splats, solving the problem of mapping arbitrary numbers of splats into fixed-size hardware texture formats.

### [Vertex-Based Leaf Node Derivation](7234-vertex-based-leaf-node-derivation.md)
[Vertex-Based Leaf Node Derivation](#7234-vertex-based-leaf-node-derivation.md) constructs leaf nodes in hierarchical volume rendering trees by mapping mesh vertices directly to bounding spheres, solving the problem of defining geometric primitives for rendering when the underlying data is a vertex cloud.

### [Gsplat Transformation](7308-gsplat-transformation.md)
The [Gsplat Transformation](#7308-gsplat-transformation.md) method applies affine and color modifications to a set of Gaussian splats, typically as part of a training or editing pipeline. It operates on a packed `Gsplat` structure, conditionally updating position, scale, orientation, and color attributes based on provided transformation parameters.

### [Optimization and Culling](8124-optimization-and-culling.md)
Not given in the sources.

### [Hybrid and Parallel Rendering](8125-hybrid-and-parallel-rendering.md)
[Hybrid and Parallel Rendering](#8125-hybrid-and-parallel-rendering.md) encompasses techniques that combine splatting with other rendering paradigms (such as ray casting or mesh rendering) or distribute the splatting workload across multiple processors to achieve performance and visual fidelity improvements.

### [Splat Sorting and Composition](8126-splat-sorting-and-composition.md)
[Splat Sorting and Composition](#8126-splat-sorting-and-composition.md) is the final stage of object-order volume rendering where depth-sorted primitives are rasterized and alpha-blended to produce the final image. It solves the problem of correct [transparency handling](#3611-order-independent-transparency-approaches.md) in splat-based rendering.

### [Noise Splats](8547-noise-splats.md)
A technique for representing multivariate data sets defined on an integer lattice by extending volume rendering to include nonhomogeneous volume representations, where varying the local amount of noise represents a separate scalar variable.

### [Splat Kernels and Footprints](8724-splat-kernels-and-footprints.md)
[Splat Kernels and Footprints](#8724-splat-kernels-and-footprints.md) define the geometric shape, spatial extent, and weighting function of the primitives used in splatting-based volume rendering. They solve the problem of how to map 3D volumetric data onto a 2D image plane while preserving visual fidelity.

### [Learning and Training Methods](9068-learning-and-training-methods.md)
This family encompasses optimization strategies for reconstructing 3D Gaussian primitives from 2D images, focusing on how the scene representation is learned and trained. It addresses the problem of parameter optimization (positions, covariances, opacities, colors) via differentiable rendering.

### [Particle and Fluid Simulation](9118-particle-and-fluid-simulation.md)
Not given in the sources.

### [Scatter Samples to Image](2779-scatter-samples-to-image.md)
A post-processing step that scatters computed sample values from arbitrary screen-space positions into a regular image grid.

### [Silhouette Splatting](8357-silhouette-splatting.md)
[Silhouette Splatting](#8357-silhouette-splatting.md) projects irregular grid cells by triangulating their convex hulls and rendering them as geometric primitives. Unlike standard splatting which treats data as point samples, this method operates on the cells between sample points.

### [Two-Pass Surfel Rendering with Enlarged Splat](12325-two-pass-surfel-rendering-with-enlarged-splat.md)
[Two-Pass Surfel Rendering with Enlarged Splat](#12325-two-pass-surfel-rendering-with-enlarged-splat.md) resolves sharp square-shaped boundary artifacts inherent in standard alpha-blended splatting by separating visibility determination from shading into two distinct passes.

### [Stroke-based splatting](12479-stroke-based-splatting.md)
[Stroke-based splatting](#12479-stroke-based-splatting.md) applies concepts of stroke-based rendering to surface-aligned splatting, shaping each object-aligned splat as a brush stroke and orienting it according to globally coherent tangent vectors to create a painterly depiction.

### [Interactive Forward Rendering with Approximate Splatting](11491-interactive-forward-rendering-with-approximate-splatting.md)
This method provides an efficient, hardware-accelerated approximation of point reprojection for high-quality free-viewpoint rendering, enabling interactive frame rates by replacing full soft rasterization with a global depth layering system.

### [World-aligned lattice octree bake](11637-world-aligned-lattice-octree-bake.md)
This method constructs a hierarchical level-of-detail (HLOD) octree for Gaussian splats aligned to world axes, grouping splats into leaves with bounded counts and ordering them by importance to enable efficient streaming and culling.

### [AstroSplat Render Modes](12010-astrosplat-render-modes.md)
[AstroSplat Render Modes](#12010-astrosplat-render-modes.md) provide two distinct visualization strategies for rendering splat fields: **Basic** mode prioritizes clarity and rendering speed, while **Enhanced** mode offers a perceptual experience with stronger depth cues.

### [Error-aware Streaming Fusion](9936-error-aware-streaming-fusion.md)
[Error-aware Streaming Fusion](#9936-error-aware-streaming-fusion.md) is a temporal stabilization technique for [dynamic 3D Gaussian](#7336-dynamic-3d-gaussians.md) Splatting that mitigates artifacts caused by warping inaccuracies and appearance variations by adaptively weighting the fusion of historical splats against current frame predictions.

### [Data Structure and Storage](10326-data-structure-and-storage.md)
Not given in the sources.

### [Particle Splatting for Density Field Construction](3916-particle-splatting-for-density-field-construction.md)
This method constructs a volumetric density field on the [CPU](#10688-naive-sdf-generation-cpu.md) by rasterizing interpolated particles into a 3D grid, enabling subsequent [ray-marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) of complex surfaces like wax. It explicitly targets CPU-side grid construction.

### [Splatch](9863-splatch.md)
[Splatch](#9863-splatch.md) is a lightweight, CPU-based ray-tracing software tool designed for the fast visualization of point-like data from cosmological simulations, such as Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) outputs.

### Extinction-based splatting
A rendering solution introduced in [S18] that uses extinction (referred to as 'density' in [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) literature) instead of the learned opacity value used in 3DGS, to analyze the difference between opacity-based and accurate volumetric rendering. For small numbers of primitives, extinction-based splatting performs better than opacity-based splatting. However, with more primitives, opacity splatting performs best [S18].

### Beta-Splatting Rendering
Loads the Beta-Splatting model from `point_cloud/iteration_{iteration}/point_cloud.ply` or `point_cloud/iteration_{iteration}/png/` directory [S19, unofficial]. It iterates over held-out test cameras obtained via `scene.getTestCameras()` [S19, unofficial]. It renders the scene for each camera using `beta_model.render(camera)` [S19, unofficial]. It clamps the rendered image and ground truth to `[0.0, 1.0]` [S19, unofficial]. It saves the render and ground truth images as PNGs in `renders/` and `gt/` directories [S19, unofficial].

### Coherent Projection (Scanline Algorithm)
A scanline algorithm that is much faster than splatting for parallel projection by scan converting depth information behind each projected polygon [S20, unofficial]. It scan converts the depth information behind each projected polygon line-by-line [S20, unofficial]. It integrates interpolated data and color samples at each scan converting step to account for raycasting-like accuracy [S20, unofficial].

### SeqAffordSplat
Performs sequential affordance reasoning on the 3DGS representation, where rendered [feature fields](#12995-feature-fields.md) encode [interaction](#41-interaction.md) probabilities over time [S21, unofficial].

### AMR Splatting with FFT
A volume rendering technique for AMR data where cells are converted into points with size information, projected to 2D, and convolved with a Gaussian kernel using FFT to produce a summation plot [S22, unofficial]. It converts AMR cells into points with additional size information depending on the AMR cell size [S22, unofficial]. It computes a different map for every AMR level involved in the camera-defined image [S22, unofficial]. For every level, it projects corresponding AMR cell center points onto the projection plane [S22, unofficial]. It transforms the 1D projected points into 2D disks by doing a convolution product with a 2D Gaussian kernel [S22, unofficial]. It performs the convolution using the Fast [Fourier Transform](#2288-fourier-transform.md) (FFT), as multiplication in Fourier space corresponds to a convolution product [S22, unofficial]. It adds all maps obtained for every level to produce the final image [S22, unofficial]. Implementation platform is CPU using Numpy's FFT module [S22, unofficial]. Grid alignment may appear on resulting images [S22, unofficial]. Solutions include increasing splatted disk/point sizes or adding a random shift to point position, though these lead to lower image quality [S22, unofficial]. It produces images close to ray-traced [Maximum Intensity Projection (MIP)](#10702-maximum-intensity-projection-mip.md) maps [S22, unofficial].

### Differentiable Forward Warping with Average Splatting
A warping strategy that estimates deformation from canonical time to another time step, ensuring smooth flows [S23]. It uses average splatting to handle the many-to-one issue where multiple source positions map to one target position [S23]. The formula is $\Vgrid {}{T}[\mathbf {p}] = \frac {\sum _{\forall \mathbf {q}\in \Vgrid {}{S}}b[\mathbf {u}]\cdot \Vgrid {}{S}[\mathbf {q}]}{\sum _{\forall \mathbf {q}\in \Vgrid {}{S}}^{}b[\mathbf {u}]}$, where $b[\mathbf {u}] = \prod \text {max}(0, 1\!-\!\left |\mathbf {u}_i \right |), {i} \in \{x,y,z\}$, and $\mathbf {u} = (\mathbf {q}+f_{\text {S}\rightarrow \text {T}}[\mathbf {q}]) - \mathbf {p}$. $x, y, z$ are three axes of the voxel grid, and $u_i \in \mathbb {R}$ is one element of the vector $\mathbf {u} \in \mathbb {R}^3$ [S23]. The many-to-one issue: Multiple positions in the source correspond to the same position in the target (e.g., when a circle shrinks) [S23]. This is handled by average splatting which fuses multiple values into one using a trilinear kernel [S23].

### gsplat
A unified high-performance API that continuously integrates low-level scheduling optimizations for constrained environments [S21, unofficial].

### Fuse-and-Refine Integration into DepthSplat
Integrate the Fuse-and-Refine module into the publicly available DepthSplat implementation [S24]. Retrain on a DL3DV subset at 128×192 resolution using 1,000 scenes with 2 input views [S24]. Evaluate on 10 test scenes with 4 input views [S24]. PSNR increases from 16.57 to 17.66, LPIS from 0.4108 to 0.4426, and LPIPS decreases from 0.4272 to 0.4019 [S24].

### REdiSplats
A method that ray traces flat 3D Gaussians aligned to mesh-based disks, allowing control of Gaussians by editing mesh vertices [S25].

### Differentiable Rendering (Forward Pass)
For each pixel $j$ with polar coordinates $(\rho_j, \theta_j)$ in the tangent plane of primitive $s_i$, compute signed distance to boundary: $\varphi_j = \rho_j - r_i(\theta_j)$ [S26]. Discard points with $\varphi_j \ge 0$ (outside primitive). Compute per-pixel opacity: $\alpha_{i,j} = o_i \cdot \max\left(0, \frac{r_i(\theta_j) - \rho_j}{r_i(\theta_j)}\right)^{\sigma_i}$ [S26]. Accumulate colors via front-to-back compositing [S26].

### 3D Splatting
A rendering technique used to generate volume-sampled tools on-the-fly for interactive sculpting operations (specifically 'sawing'), preventing object space aliasing while achieving interactive speed [S27, unofficial]. It generates the volume-sampled tool on-the-fly using a user interface [S27, unofficial]. It renders the generated tool using 3D splatting to prevent aliasing and maintain interactive frame rates [S27, unofficial].

### Point-Based Neural Renderer Architecture
A neural network that encodes rasterized point clouds from multiple input views, pools features with inductive bias for visibility and temporal smoothing, and decodes them to generate the final rendering [S28]. It generates attribute layers for each view: input-view colors and optimized latent features reprojected to the novel view using point splatting [S28]. It encodes each view in a feature space of F dimensions using convolutional residual blocks with shared weights across all input views [S28]. It applies weighted average pooling to produce a single F-channel image using the final weights w [S28]. It decodes the pooled features using consecutive convolutional residual blocks to generate the final rendering [S28]. Feature space dimension F is typically 64 [S28]. Unlike previous [neural renderers](#11612-point-based-neural-renderer-architecture.md), this architecture allows changing the number of selected views without retraining because weighted average pooling normalizes the sum of weights per pixel [S28].

### Probabilistic Depth Testing for Point-Based Rendering
A method to determine visibility in novel views by incorporating depth uncertainty from MVS reconstruction, replacing hard visibility tests with soft probabilistic weights to prevent discarding valuable information from noisy data [S28].

### Hit Pixel Count Renderer
Project Gaussians: call GSPlatRenderer.project with means3D, scales, rotations, viewpoint_camera, scaling_modifier, block_size, extra_projection_kwargs to get xys, depths, radii, conics, comp, num_tiles_hit, cov3d [S29, unofficial]. Anti-aliasing: if anti_aliased is True, multiply opacities by comp[:, None] [S29, unofficial]. Compute hit pixel count: call hit_pixel_count with xys, depths, radii, conics, num_tiles_hit, opacities, img_height, img_width, block_width; return count, opacity_score, alpha_score, visibility_score [S29, unofficial]. scaling_modifier is float = 1.0 [S29, unofficial]. anti_aliased is bool = True [S29, unofficial]. block_size is int = 16 [S29, unofficial].

### A-buffer Blending for Splatting
A blending technique using an A-buffer to remove high-frequency noise at patch boundaries and simulate a painterly effect while preserving individual splat curvature [S30]. For all pixels $pix_{uv}$: If all fragments are sorted, retrieve the result from the A-buffer. If not, perform a step of bubble sort on the sorted fragments, perform an alpha blend step, update the A-buffer, and set the result [S30]. Two-pass weighted Gaussian blur is implemented as an alternative for moving objects or camera navigation, where A-buffering might be too expensive [S30].

## Background
Splatting was first proposed by Westover [S5, unofficial]. It is an object-order approach, contrasting with ray-casting which is image-order [S4, unofficial][S14, unofficial]. The term is derived from the analogy of throwing snowballs (volume elements) at a wall (image plane), where each snowball leaves a fuzzy circular mark (footprint) [S6, unofficial]. Splatting is considered one of the four main paradigms of volume rendering [S9, book]. It is particularly effective for generating [X-ray projection](#1492-forward-projection-atx.md) images from volumes, as the summation of pre-integrated reconstruction kernels is faster and more accurate than ray-casting for this specific output [S3, unofficial]. The method is also used in [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md), where millions of 3D Gaussians are optimized by tweaking parameters until the rendered image matches a real image [S5, unofficial][S13, unofficial].
